title: The cluster declares polyhedra week, and people post entries
summary: The cluster names its weeks after whatever it is making. On Sat 14 Nov @yonderdavid.bsky.social prefaced a new video with "it's arguably still chimera-vocal-synth week". On Mon 16 Nov a small account in the cluster, @oscillatory.net, quote-posted a link about a newly described polyhedron with "it's polyhedra week" (15 likes). On Tue 17 Nov @norvid-studies.bsky.social quote-posted @yonderdavid.bsky.social's video of instruments made of polyhedra with "it's polyhedra week now, lock in" (42 likes), and an hour later @shimmermathlabs.com told the video's maker "polyhedron week has just begun and you may have already won it". By Wed 18 Nov posts were being offered as entries: a morning mug with polyhedra on it, answered by another mug with a hand-drawn twenty-sided shape; six pieces from a small account's origami collection "for Simcluster Polyhedron Week™" (38 likes, 5 reposts); a piece of music "for polyhedra week"; and one member promising a "chimera week entry" a few weeks late.

posts.text: Very well, it's arguably still chimera-vocal-synth week, so I can fix that. The cat voice sim joins a quartet and instruments that get their sound from physical models.

posts.text: Improptu posting some old stuff from my origami collection for Simcluster Polyhedron Week™, see descriptions in alt text
alt: Woven Dodecahedron, a classic model by David Brill of the British Origami Society; six strips that use one golden rectangle in its entirety. Maybe my favorite modular origami design. Unlike the average sort this is also *very* sturdy, you could outright play street hockey with it (I've tested)
Also a model of Brill's, roughly an omnisunken rhombic hexecontahedron. Technically, not a polyhedron as much as a net / skeleton for one, ideally folded this would have zero volume.
The classic rhombic dodecahedron; unit design by Nick Robinson. I have a whole pile of these stashed for demonstrating / testing the spacefilling property
Tiny "harlequin cube" showing the full symmetry elements of the octahedral group. Just six pieces that are mild variants of the classic Sonobe unit, much simpler than the finished model looks like.

A partially-sunken cube unit of my own design. Looks like 12 units but is actually just 6, each square face and its indents are one piece. I've wanted to use the principle from this to develop also the 24× sunken version similar to the previous cube, I never finished that project alas.

Another design of my own: kind of a half-unit for a sunken deltoidal icositetrahedron; this is one sheet, kind of a quadruple cootie catcher (though I suppose a smaller unit might make a sharper whole polyhedron). Also serves as a rosette for decorating gifts!

sensitive: No post on this card carries a flag from the tool. (1) Two small accounts, both cluster members: @oscillatory.net (274 followers), who named the week, and @oszillate.bsky.social (75 followers), who posted the origami. Both are here for something they did well (R7); the second is the smallest account on any card in this lane. Other threads by @oscillatory.net this week sit inside a story the digest flags and are not used. (2) "chimera" is the vocal synth this show is made with, and another "chimera week" post in the window is by the show's owner; that post is left out so that the show is not its own subject, and the two "chimera" lines here are listed only as the naming habit. (3) @heartpunk.com's line has 0 likes, and her other posts this week include her age, money and hormones, which are out of bounds; only this one line is carded. (4) @norvid-studies.bsky.social and @samantha.wiki are marked by the tool as having spoken in the previous episode, and @shimmermathlabs.com as shown: their posts may be shown; the first two do not speak. (5) Left out: a reply calling someone else's morning greeting "an entry for polyhedra week... but not a good one" (a tease at another account), and a mug photo that shows the poster's tattooed arm (appearance). (6) "gar week" in the digest's list is one member quoting an outside scientist's annual event; it is not a cluster week and is not carded. (7) The things made for the week belong to the made lane; this card is the naming and the entering.
